answer: I would like to talk about someone at my office whose manners I have always admired. The most polite person I know is an older colleague of mine, whose manners are almost old-fashioned in the best possible way. I got to know him when I joined the education consultancy, because he was the one who showed me how everything worked in my first week, when I was nervous and constantly making small mistakes. No matter how busy or stressed he is, he always greets everyone warmly and remembers small details about their lives, like a colleague's child's exams or someone's sick parent. What makes his politeness feel genuine rather than forced is that it is completely [[consistent]]; he treats the office cleaner with exactly the same respect as the director. He is also a wonderful listener, never interrupting, which is [[a rarity]] these days. With students and parents, he stays unfailingly respectful, even when they are rude or impatient on the phone. I have noticed that his [[courtesy]] has a ripple effect, making the whole team more considerate towards one another. In meetings, even when he disagrees, he does so [[tactfully]], so no one ever feels attacked. As for how I feel about him, I genuinely think politeness is an underrated quality, and he is living proof of how much smoother it makes everyday interactions. Honestly, being around him quietly reminds me to mind my own manners, and I think I have become a slightly better person for working beside him.

followUps.q: Do you think people are less polite nowadays?
followUps.answer: In some ways, yes, particularly online, where people say things they would never say face to face. But I still see plenty of [[everyday courtesy]] in my town, especially towards older people.

followUps.q: Were you taught to be polite as a child?
followUps.answer: Very much so. My parents were quite strict about greeting elders properly and saying thank you, and I am grateful now, because good manners have helped me a great deal at work.

note: Set him at my consultancy and added how I know him, examples of his politeness with students and a reflective close; replaced plain mark 'rare' with 'a rarity'.
